Capacity strengthening of WROs through knowledge building; L&A capacities are essential for WHRDs and WROs to input, participate and influence ideas, agendas,policies, and institutions. Knowledge Building on Anti-Rights Actors and Agendas - publication of Rights at Risk: Time for Change Report & associated knowledge productsThe report draws on the “know your enemy” strategy and helped equip feminist movements to better understand and confront anti-rights threats. It also had impact amongst other civil society allies and policy makers - bringing a more nuanced, political, intersectional, feminist analysis that was hitherto lacking in discussions of anti-rights trends. It helped establish the “opposition monitoring” field of work as a recognized area of work and is now even reaching a more mainstream narrative around the ‘backlash’. 88 + 143 people downloaded and accessed via our webiste a key knowledge resource. "Two exchanges (April, July 2022) focused on alliance-building across domestic workers and feminist movements intersecting struggles and identities. It was a closed exchange, with a total of 26 participants, and brought together domestic workers from across regions from the first exchange and a select group of feminist activists and thinkers from different areas (i.e. economic justice activists centering care work and public services, migrant women, people with disabilities, queer, lgbtqi+, black and indigenous feminisms, informal workers and other labor rights feminist activists, among others). Participant feedback included affirmation that “such spaces are limited and incongruent with their urgent need. I found the space very insightful and productive.” 26 activists took part in two exchanges focussed on alliance building across domestic workers and feminist movements."AWID crafted feminist narratives on economic alternatives so we can showcase and visibilise these realities via the launch of a multimedia storytelling project in October 2022: https://awid.org/feminist-economies-we-love. We supported learning on Feminist Economic Alternatives by raising awareness and interest around the subject of alternative feminist economies and sharing specific examples and models from around the world. The overall intention is to inspire feminist movements and demonstrate that more just and sustainable ways of organizing our economies and societies are possible (in alignment with outcome 3). By doing so, the project aims to counter mainstream narratives that exclude viable economic alternatives that defy and resist market-capitalism as we know it and showcase the stories of inspiring collectives around the world. - Caring Economies: featuring the stories of Ocupacao 9 de Julho (Brasil), Asociación de Mujeres Afrodescendientes del Norte del Cauca (Colombia) and Metzineres (Spain) (63 plays)- Land and Agro-Ecology: featuring the story of Nous Sommes la Solution (West Africa) (23 plays)- Feminist Cooperativism: featuring the story of the Nadia Echazu textile cooperative (Argentina) (23 plays)- Feminist Union Organizing: featuring the stories of Soldiarity Network Union (Georgia) and the OTRAS Union (Spain) (35 plays)"Partners: The International Network of People who Use Drugs (INPUD), Harm Reduction International (HRI), Metzineres, Calala, Women and Harm Reduction International Network (WHRIN), Eurasian Harm Reduction Association (EHRA) and Eurasian Network of People who Use Drugs (ENPUD)This was a learning session developed through a cautious and intentional co-creation process with our partners. 12 funding institutions present (against the session's initial target of 10) (yet only 6 stayed for the full 2 hours) and a diverse group of about 20 activists speaking to and with them. The session itself and the process leading up to it were really strong on movements’ engagement, power sharing and strengthening AWID’s relationships with diverse groups of feminists resisting the war on drugs. And on-going communication with partners, including invitation to AWID to serve as a technical partner in a new project led by Metzineres aimed at building cross movement solidarity amongst women who use drugs and feminist movements. A number of partners to continue work with AWID for the Feminists Resisting the War on Drugs Teach In (October 13) and partners from the session attended.

"1. 150 WROs taking part in CSW68 community evening2. 1174 responses to the WITM survey3. 4100 Forum participants - in person, virtual and hybridThe 2500 target is the initial estimate number of AWID Forum participants.""150 feminists attended the Community Evening to network, connect, heal and find joy in the midst of their activism during CSW68. In the mid-term recview, CMI! partners identified the vibrancy and health of their organisations and movements as a critical pillar of sustainability. Member events such as this contribute to this. “A lot of times in our work as feminist and as organizers, we end up feeling really lonely and we're present in a lot of spaces that don't cater to us and don't accommodate us. But when we're present at an AWID event like the one that we attended today, it really felt like being at home and it felt like being with our people who are really value aligned and that understood the issues and the places that we were coming from.” Yosra Soltan, WHRD-MENA, 12th March, 2024, AWID Feminist Community Evening, NYC, CSW 68" "The survey resulted in 1,174 responses from organizations across 129 countries. Notably, 80% of respondents work at the local or national level in countries in the Global South. We successfully reached diverse movements, including historically marginalized groups such as those working on climate, disability justice, trans rights, harm reduction, and more. Accessibility was a key consideration, and we piloted the survey to ensure that individuals with diverse hearing, movement, sight, and cognitive abilities could participate fully. Initially, the survey was translated into six languages, Arabic, English, French, Portuguese, Russian, and Spanish, and later into an additional six South Asian languages to further widen its reach."

Nearly 1,500 feminists came together virtually at convenings designed to build & strengthen learning and solidarity and build cross-movement alliances.●Curated conversations on “What has Feminism Got to do with it?”, “Movement as Healing: an online convening of 30 healers and activists (by invitation only)”, and “No Borders, No Walls: Feminist for Abolition” (23 participants).●A month-long feminist festival where 130 activists from 43 countries held 40 sessions to celebrate and transform movements. There were 2,800+ views on our YouTube channel, and the hashtag #FeministFestival reached two million people over six months (including the lead-up and post-festival period).(June) Publication: Second Trends report: Rights at Risk, Time for Action - downloaded 225+ times. >60% are from Grassroots, Social movements, NGOs and/or INGOs. 50% say they plan to use the resource as a tool for advocacy. ●Also published a policy brief in November to continue building knowledge on how to counter the strategies & tactics of anti-rights actors.Strengthened the collective power of young feminists by supporting their strategizing, organizing and learning during the GEF process, where young feminists were formally involved and also held a 3-day Young Feminist Unconference (June) in Paris attended by over 100 young feminists."Constituency engagement taking place in a safe space for dialogue and action at local, national, regional and cross-regional/global levelsSpaces created that support and enable self-organised, collective and community-based protection strategies "Number of members who took part in more than 1 activityNumber of activists at the three portals connecting with each other, contributing to movement building."Number of activists at portal hubs- Bangalore = 30- Nairobi = 34- New York = 30""2. Outcomes 2024 " 4,100 feminists attended the AWID Forum from 160 countries gathered in-person in Bangkok and virtually - online and through Hubs in eight cities worldwide.A total of 3,379 people participated in-person at the Forum from over 160 countries. This represented a 35% increase in the in-person attendance from our original plan of 2,500.Approximately 700 people participated in the Forum remotely, either attending the hybrid or online-only sessions, or at one of the eight self-organized Hubs across cities including Accra, Mexico City, Kingston, and Nairobi. Over 85% of participants were attending their first Forum.Young feminists were a significant presence, with 1 in 5 participants under the age of 30, ensuring that their voices and realities were strongly felt throughout the convening.""Total number of AWID Members as of 31 Dec 2024 = 8518; this is the highest number of AWID member so far. in 2021 The space defended was space UN space for more feminist movement building and advocacy 2023 Being about to host and facilitate such spaces and convenings is a very important resource when it comes to strengthening feminist movements and building movements.Feminists seems to be in the 'defendig space' mode of operations in 2023 for most of 2023 so being able to support partners and allies to create space and hold them for strategic discussions is exceedingly important in the current context. These include:1. The Nov 2023 in person OURs meeting in Naivash - 23 participants, both a mix of long-time OURs members and newcomers. By the end of the convening, the coalition reiterated the value and need to keep building and maintaining a trust-based working relationship, that despite the challenges posed by the anti-rights context, the OURS as a feminist collective has the will and capacity to analyze the scope of these challenges and produce new tactics, and coordination and information exchange remain key.2. Creating space for feminists to shout There is no place for anti-trans agendas in the UN: To hold the current SR VAW accountable. AWID released a public statement on 23 May, as a strong demonstration of feminist solidarity with trans people’s rights and recalled our commitment to human rights and the principles of bodily autonomy for all, as well as the importance of the mandate of the UN SR VAW. Over 1700 organizations and individuals signed the public statement, which has been repeatedly affirmed by funders and allies in the multilateral spaces for its content, clarity, and usefulness for internal advocacy. This action was much needed as part of solidarity and also calling out the harm statements by the SR VAW is doing. An important added value of this work is the formalization of the civil society partnership spontaneously created in the process. AWID maintain regular communication on ways to counter trans-exclusionary trends and put trans rights firmly on international feminist agendas. 3.

Expanded and more nuanced understanding of gender: AWID organized several events to launch the second Trends report by AWID and the Observatory on the Universality of Rights (OURs) - Rights at Risk: Time for Action - and its key messages with as many audiences as possible, including during the UN CSW 65, at the Global Philanthropy Project’s Shimmering Solidarity Summit, and through a press briefing in partnership with openDemocracy 50.50. Preliminary data from users downloading the report suggest that the majority are using the report to learn about anti-rights strategies and feminist resistance. At the same time, about half intend to use the resource as a tool for advocacy. AWID has developed an eight-page brief to make our analysis more accessible, encouraging policymakers to engage with the content and access the full report. It will be a useful advocacy tool for activists. We repeatedly hear positive feedback about the report's usefulness from UN officials and mandate holders, international development agencies, feminists, women's rights and LGBTQI+ rights organizations. 2023"We continue to advocate at the multilateral level to ensure all UN actors who need to be alerted have been informed, understand our analysis, and are prompted to take action to counter anti-rights tides. This includes regular participation in UN Human Rights Council sessions, in the Commission on the Status of Women (CSW) and coordination with feminist and WROs organisations who engage in national, regional and global advocacy.
